claims.text: TC4 is an unmodified Ti-6Al-4V alloy with an alpha-plus-beta dual-phase microstructure.
Untreated TC4 has low surface hardness and poor wear resistance.
Nitrogen ion implantation will incorporate nitrogen into the near-surface region of TC4.
Nitrogen ion implantation will form a hardened nitrided surface layer consisting primarily of TiN.
The intervention will produce nanoscale TiN precipitates.
The intervention will produce a gradient-hardened surface layer.
Nitrogen implantation will increase dislocation density in the surface region.
Implanted nitrogen atoms react with titanium in the surface region to form TiN.
TiN acts as a hard ceramic phase that increases surface hardness.
The nitrided layer provides a wear-resistant barrier.
Surface-localized implantation preserves the ductility and toughness of the TC4 interior.
Nitrogen implantation is predicted to increase TC4 surface hardness by approximately 30–50% relative to untreated TC4.
Nitrogen implantation is predicted to reduce TC4 wear rate relative to untreated TC4 under similar test conditions.
Untreated TC4 has a standard Vickers hardness of approximately 350–400 HV.
The anticipated improvement applies from room temperature to approximately 300°C under high-contact-stress conditions.
Excessive implantation fluence or energy could cause over-nitriding, brittleness, or delamination.
The mechanism of nitriding is well established.
The exact hardness and wear improvement for ion-implanted TC4 depends on empirical optimization of processing conditions.
Implanted and untreated TC4 samples will be compared using Vickers hardness measurements, pin-on-disc wear tests, and surface microscopy under otherwise identical conditions.
The hypothesis is falsified if implantation produces less than a 10% hardness increase and no lower wear rate than untreated TC4.
